title: Ulyana and the Drop
premise: Rafael Underhill, a fixer for the Meridian Trust — an embassy that exists on no map and answers to no flag — has been unraveling since 'the incident,' an operation she can't fully remember. When a burner phone rings with the voice of her dead handler, Ulyana, she learns the Trust's training program manufactured its own operatives through erased memories, and Rafael is one of them. Hunting the network that made her, she discovers Ulyana is alive, running a counter-conspiracy that wants Rafael as its weapon. In the end, Rafael refuses both masters: she burns the Trust's archive publicly, lets Ulyana vanish, and walks out of the embassy that never existed carrying only her own name.
about_author: Xanthe Sterling is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade in cities that appear on no itineraries. She writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are the last thing they lose.

chapters.title: The Embassy That Isn't
chapters.summary: Rafael Underhill's POV. A routine cleanup job in Vienna — scrubbing a diplomat who never existed from three databases — goes sideways when Rafael finds her own handwriting in a file dated after the incident. Insomnia-frayed and paranoid, she pockets the page. Beat: dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Burner at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A phone she's never seen rings inside her safehouse; the voice is Ulyana Kessler, her handler, dead eleven months by official record. Ulyana says four words — 'they trained you too' — before the line dies. Beat: vertigo; the ground of Rafael's identity cracks open.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She reports nothing and investigates alone, breaking Trust protocol for the first time. Flashbacks surface unbidden: a white room, a metronome, someone counting down. Her deputy, Osei, notices her slipping. Beat: isolation deepening as she chooses secrets over safety.

chapters.title: The White Room
chapters.summary: Split POV begins: chapters alternate between Rafael and Ulyana, hiding in Riga. Ulyana fakes her own death's paperwork while watching Rafael's movements through the burner. We learn Ulyana defected from the Trust's 'Gardener' program after seeing what it did to recruits. Beat: cold resolve; two women circling the same wound.

chapters.title: Osei's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Osei confronts her with evidence he's kept for years: forty operatives with gaps in their histories, all routed through the same clinic in Tbilisi. He offers partnership but warns the Trust audits loyalty biometrically now. Beat: wary alliance; trust as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Tbilisi Clinic
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The clinic is a shell, but a basement server still holds session logs — including Rafael's own voice reciting things she doesn't remember saying. She copies everything and triggers a silent alarm she doesn't see. Beat: horror of self-recognition; the past becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Trust's internal auditor, Voss, flags Rafael and orders a retrieval team. Ulyana intercepts the order and must decide whether to warn Rafael or use her as bait to reach Voss. Beat: moral compromise; Ulyana proves she can be ruthless too.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ambushed in Prague, Rafael survives only because the attackers hesitate — they recognize something in her face, call her by another name, 'Sable.' She kills one, wounds another, and realizes the program gave her skills she never chose. Beat: violence as revelation; power she didn't ask for.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, fractured with recovered memory. Fragments return: Sable was her designation, the incident was a botched erasure that left her half-wiped, and Ulyana signed off on the procedure. Betrayal lands harder than the bullets did. Beat: rage; the rescuer revealed as accomplice.

chapters.title: Confrontation in Riga
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Rafael tracks Ulyana down; guns drawn, truths exchanged. Ulyana admits she authorized the erasure to save Rafael from execution after Sable refused an order — then went underground to dismantle the program. Beat: fury curdling into reluctant understanding.

chapters.title: The Gardener Files
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She shows Rafael the full archive: the Gardener program built deniable operatives across twelve embassies-that-don't-exist, and Voss is its architect, not its auditor. The Trust's directorate is compromised or complicit. Beat: scale reveal; this is bigger than one woman's stolen past.

chapters.title: Osei's Choice
chapters.summary: Osei's POV (first departure). Summoned before the directorate, Osei lies about Rafael's whereabouts and feels the noose tighten. He passes her location to Voss under duress, believing he's protecting her from worse. Beat: betrayal born of love; good intentions as ammunition.

chapters.title: Safehouse Fire
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Voss's team torches the Riga safehouse; Ulyana is captured covering Rafael's escape. Wounded and hunted, Rafael realizes every asset she trusted is either dead, turned, or lying. Beat: rock bottom; grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. For the first time since the incident, Rafael sleeps — four hours, dreamless — and wakes clear-eyed. She stops running and starts planning: to burn the network, she needs the archive's second copy inside Meridian headquarters itself. Beat: turning point; exhaustion transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: Recruitment of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She assembles the program's other survivors — Sable-adjacent operatives with holes in their memories — using the Tbilisi logs as proof. Some join for justice, some for revenge. Beat: found family among the erased; power offered back to its victims.

chapters.title: Inside Meridian
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Using credentials Osei smuggles out in a act of partial redemption, the team infiltrates headquarters during a directorate summit. Voss expects them; the operation is a stage he built. Beat: trap closing; the hunters realize they are prey.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael and Voss, face to face. He offers restoration: full memory returned, career intact, Ulyana released — if Rafael delivers the survivor network to him. He reveals the incident wasn't an accident; Rafael broke her own programming once before. Beat: temptation; the devil offers her herself.

chapters.title: What Sable Refused
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, memory flooding back whole. Years ago, Sable refused to execute a child witness — the first crack in her conditioning. The incident was punishment, not malfunction. Rafael understands now: her rebellion predates her amnesia. Beat: identity reclaimed; she was always herself.

chapters.title: The Burn
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. Rafael double-crosses Voss: instead of the network, she broadcasts the Gardener archive to every intelligence service on earth during the summit. Firefights in the marble halls; Osei takes a bullet shielding the uplink; Ulyana breaks her own cell. Beat: catharsis through fire; justice outside the law, paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Voss, exposed, is consumed by his own masters — the directorate erases him the way they erase everyone. Governments scramble; embassies that don't exist start to, very loudly. The survivors scatter with new names they choose themselves. Beat: costly victory; the world rearranged.

chapters.title: Two Names
chapters.summary: Rafael and Ulyana, final meeting at a Riga harbor. Ulyana offers partnership in whatever comes next; Rafael declines — not forgiveness, but release. They part as equals, each keeping one name and surrendering the other. Beat: bittersweet closure; love without ownership.

chapters.title: Underhill, Awake
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue. Months later, in a city with no operational value, Rafael sleeps through the night and wakes to an ordinary morning. A burner phone sits in her drawer, switched off. She leaves it there. Beat: peace earned, vigilance retained; identity as a daily choice.
